openings.claim: A deliberately disconnected digest comparator and evidence ledger can still deliver honest unresolved intervals, but will lose supported localization relative to an intact handoff.
openings.delta: Change only the handoff carrier: compare supplied digests at matching artifact boundaries, then send the ledger an unordered equality/inequality multiset without boundary or record identifiers. Preserve the comparison function and the ledger function. The ledger independently catalogs supplied record identifiers, stages and missing fields; it must not rematch anonymous results, reread digests to reconstruct comparisons, or infer definite divergence from the detached results.
openings.prediction: Against the nearest rival, the same workflow with boundary-and-record-linked comparison results, the disconnected variant should produce more unresolved intervals and fewer correct definite stages. Timestamp inversion should not justify stage reordering in either variant. This difference is conjectural, not a measured effect.
openings.probe: Use one disjoint three-pair subset per variant, identical manifest ordering, frozen outputs and inspection logs. Each pair receives an earliest supported stage or explicit unresolved interval, supplied record references and a bounded next check. The disconnected variant can report the manifest-ordered ingest-to-export interval with catalogued references; its next check names a manifest-listed missing boundary record for inspection, without executing a repair. Remove one transform record from each of two pairs during final review. Freeze outputs before opening the two sealed answer sheets; compare supported localization, correctness, interval coverage and inspection counts within twenty additional minutes. Unequal subset difficulty limits causal comparison.
assumptions: The supplied local script can discard handoff labels while retaining both functions and their independent records.
Defeat: any reconstructed handoff, unsupported definite claim, missing-record nonexecution inference, interval excluding the revealed boundary, or more than twelve manual inspections per pair.

Capacity requires automated extraction within sixty analyst minutes; the cap alone does not establish feasibility. If extraction cannot finish, retain unresolved intervals and report the resource failure.
Which pairs lose records and how the sealed sheets cover the subsets are unspecified; do not invent either.

assessment: Probe only. The interface break is intentionally retained; the candidate offers conservative traceability, not demonstrated localization performance or deployment readiness.
